name: Installed related apps
plain: A page can ask whether its own native app, store app or installed web app is on this device.
meaning: It answers only for apps the site has a verified link to, but that is enough to tell a customer from a stranger. Chrome 140 added same scope installed PWAs on desktop.

chrome.note: Same scope installed PWAs on desktop from Chrome 140

chrome_android.note: Reports installed Android apps with a verified assetlinks link

data.metric: A page can ask whether its own native app, store app or installed web app is on this device.

fields.name: platform
fields.range: play, chromeos_play, webapp, windows, f-droid, amazon

limits.headline: Can tell whether the site's own app is installed, but not list your apps
limits.user_action: None, the page reads it silently
can: Check for the site's own Android, Windows or web app
Skip a "get our app" banner for people who have it
See an installed PWA of the same scope on desktop Chrome
cannot: List every app on the device
Check apps the site has no verified link to
Work in Safari, Firefox or on iPhone
limits.differs: Chromium only. Android needs a Digital Asset Links file that proves the site and app belong together.

story.what_it_is: The page can learn whether the site's own app is installed on your device.

marketing.name: Detect your installed apps
marketing.pitch: Lets a site decide whether to show an install banner or hand off to the app.

story.for_you: You never see this. A shop that already has its app on your phone may stop nagging you to install it, or send you into the app.
story.for_makers: Makers avoid promoting an app people already have, and route returning customers into the app.

use_cases.example: A retailer hides its app banner when its Android app is already installed.
A social site offers Open in app instead of Install.

risks: Reveals customer status with no prompt
story.android_note: Chrome on Android reads installed apps that carry a verified assetlinks.json relationship.

technical_bounds: Android needs a verified Digital Asset Links relationship
Safari, Firefox and iOS do not implement it

legit_uses: Hand off to the native app
abuse: Tell customers of one brand from another

history.change: Same scope installed PWAs reported on desktop
